html:
The capital of Mauritania, built from 1958 near a small fort on the Atlantic coast, because the colony had been ruled from Saint-Louis in Senegal and had no city of its own.

Moktar Ould Daddah chose the site as a meeting point between the Moorish north and the black African south. Planned for about 15,000 people, it grew fast when the Sahel droughts of the 1970s and 1980s killed herds and drove nomads into tents and shanties on its edges. It now has over a million people. Sand and rising sea threaten parts of the city.
sum: The capital of Mauritania, built from 1958 near a small fort on the Atlantic coast, because the colony had been ruled from Saint-Louis in Senegal and had no city of its own.
